reason: Start with the kidney's filter, where small substances leave the blood before recovery.
expectation: The capillary tufts and capsules will form a filtration unit, though the details remain to be shown.

alternatives.reason: The tubule transport machinery is also needed, but filtration is a natural starting point.

effect: The filter also admits useful substances, so the next priority is a selective recovery route.
reaction: The distinction between filtering and reclaiming useful material is clear and interesting.
reason: Add transport proteins to the tubules to build the machinery for selective recovery.
expectation: The tubules will gain routes for reclaiming glucose, salts and water, though their connection to blood may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The collecting route is also needed, but recovery follows naturally from filtration.

effect: The tubules now have selective transport machinery; they still need a blood route and connection to the filter.
reaction: The placement of the carrier and pump makes recovery more concrete.
reason: Connect the recovery tubules to blood vessels so reclaimed substances have a route back to circulation.
expectation: The tubules will be associated with surrounding blood vessels that can receive recovered substances.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the filter is also necessary, but I want to establish the recovery route first.

effect: The recovery tubules now have surrounding capillaries and open connections for the filters.
reaction: The open connections make the next assembly clear.
reason: Connect the filtering units to the recovery route so filtered fluid can enter the tubules.
expectation: The filter and recovery tubules will form a connected kidney unit, with vessels available for returning reclaimed substances.

effect: The filters and recovery tubules now form connected units with a blood return route; urine drainage remains to be built.
reaction: The continuous blood path makes the assembly easier to follow.
reason: Connect the collecting ducts to the kidney drainage funnels as the next part of the urine route.
expectation: The ducts will feed into the drainage funnels, leaving a connection to the ureters to be made.

alternatives.reason: The ureters and bladder also need connecting, but I prefer to build outward from the kidney.

effect: The collecting ducts now drain toward a renal pelvis with an open ureter outlet.
reaction: The pictured route makes the remaining connection clear.
reason: Connect the filtering and recovery units to the collecting trees to complete the kidney's internal route.
expectation: The tubules will feed into the collecting ducts, leaving the urine outlet to be connected.

alternatives.reason: The downstream ureters and bladder also need joining, but I prefer to finish the kidney first.

effect: The kidneys now contain connected filtering, recovery and collecting routes, while urine drainage remains to be connected.
reaction: The separate blood and tubular routes clarify where reclaimed material and urine go.
reason: Connect the ureters to the bladder and urethra to build the downstream drainage route.
expectation: The ureters will lead into the bladder, with the urethra providing an outlet; the kidneys will still need connecting.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters to the kidneys first would also advance the drainage route.
